title: An elementary etale neighbourhood splits off the finite part of a separated locally finite type morphism (Stacks 02LP)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $s\in S$, and assume that the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has at most finitely many isolated points (points $x$ with $\{x\}$ open in $X_s$). Then there exist a scheme $U$, an etale morphism $\varphi:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ such that the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $\varphi$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism (an elementary etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$), and a decomposition $U\times_SX=W\sqcup V$ of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] into two disjoint open (hence also closed) subschemes $W,V$, such that the composite $V\hookrightarrow U\times_SX\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and the fibre $W_u=W\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ of $W\to U$ at $u$ has no isolated points. In particular, if $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set, then $W_u=\emptyset$, i.e. no point of $W$ maps to $u$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02LP (lemma-etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part), line 12172, with its proof (from Lemma 02LN, lemma-etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part-technical, choosing x_1,...,x_n all isolated points of X_s and V the union of the V_i)

proof.text: *Notation and the points.* Let $\iota:X_s\to X$ be the first projection; it is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto $f^{-1}(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], in particular injective. By hypothesis the set of isolated points of $X_s$ (points $\xi$ with $\{\xi\}$ open in $X_s$) is finite; list it without repetition as $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$ ($n\ge0$) and put $x_i=\iota(\xi_i)\in X$. Then $x_1,\dots,x_n$ are pairwise distinct ($\iota$ injective), $f(x_i)=s$, and $\xi_i$ is the unique point of $X_s$ over $x_i$, which is isolated in $X_s$. Moreover, for a point $\xi\in X_s$: $\iota(\xi)\in\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$ if and only if $\xi$ is isolated in $X_s$.

source.place: Lemma 02LP, proof (line 12192): 'choosing $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ the complete set of isolated points of $X_s$'

proof.text: *Applying 02LN.* As $f$ is locally of finite type and separated and $x_1,\dots,x_n$ are pairwise distinct points over $s$ isolated in $X_s$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-splits-off-isolated-points-technical] gives an elementary etale neighbourhood $\varphi:(U,u)\to(S,s)$ ($\varphi$ etale, $\varphi(u)=s$, $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ an isomorphism) and pairwise disjoint open subschemes $W,V_1,\dots,V_n$ covering $X_U=U\times_SX$, with projections $p:X_U\to X$, $q:X_U\to U$, such that each $V_i\to U$ is finite, has exactly one point $v_i$ over $u$ with $p(v_i)=x_i$, and (iv) no point $w\in W$ with $q(w)=u$ has $p(w)\in\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$. (For $n=0$ the node allows $U=S$, $u=s$, $W=X_U$.)

*The decomposition $U\times_SX=W\sqcup V$ with $V\to U$ finite.* Put $V=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_n$, an open subscheme of $X_U$. Since $W,V_1,\dots,V_n$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $X_U$, $W$ and $V$ are disjoint opens with $W\cup V=X_U$, so each is the complement of the other and both are open and closed: $X_U=W\amalg V$. The open subscheme $V$ is the union of the pairwise disjoint opens $V_i$, so it is the coproduct $V_1\amalg\dots\amalg V_n$ of schemes (a morphism out of $V$ is the same as a family of morphisms out of the $V_i$, since morphisms of schemes glue along an open cover and the $V_i$ do not meet), and $q|_V:V\to U$ is the morphism induced by the finite morphisms $q|_{V_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] (a coproduct of two finite morphisms to $U$ is finite), applied $n-1$ times by induction on $n$ to $(V_1\amalg\dots\amalg V_{k})\amalg V_{k+1}$, $q|_V$ is finite when $n\ge1$. If $n=0$ then $V=\emptyset$, and $\emptyset\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: it is affine, the preimage of every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ being $\emptyset=\operatorname{Spec}0$, and $0$ is a finite $R$-module.

*The fibre of $X_U$ at $u$ is $X_s$.* Let $(X_U)_u=X_U\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ be the fibre of $q$ at $u$, with projections $\iota':(X_U)_u\to X_U$ and $\pi':(X_U)_u\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$, and $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ the second projection. Since $q$ is the base change of $f$ along $\varphi$ (the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]), [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] gives a morphism $h:(X_U)_u\to X_s$ with $\iota\circ h=p\circ\iota'$ such that $(X_U)_u$ with $h,\pi'$ is a fibre product $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ along $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$, $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ the map induced by $\varphi$. As $r$ is an isomorphism, $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$ is an isomorphism, and the base change $h$ of an isomorphism is an isomorphism (the pair $(\mathrm{id}_{X_s},\operatorname{Spec}(r)^{-1}\circ\pi)$ also makes the square cartesian, so $h$ is the canonical isomorphism between two fibre products). In particular $h$ is a homeomorphism, and for $w\in(X_U)_u$: $p(\iota'(w))=\iota(h(w))$.

source.place: Lemma 02LL, proof (line 11998): 'Since $\kappa(s)=\kappa(u)$ the fibre $(X_U)_u=X_s$', used implicitly in the proof of Lemma 02LP

proof.text: *$W_u$ as an open of $(X_U)_u$; its points.* The fibre $W_u=W\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ of $q|_W$ at $u$ is, by pasting cartesian squares [def-pc-fibre-product], $W\times_{X_U}(X_U)_u$, and since $W\subseteq X_U$ is an open subscheme, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] it is the open subscheme $\iota'^{-1}(W)$ of $(X_U)_u$, with the restriction of $\iota'$ as its projection to $W$. Key claim: for every $w\in W_u$, the point $h(w)\in X_s$ is not isolated in $X_s$. Indeed $\iota'(w)\in W$ and $q(\iota'(w))=u$, so by step 2 (iv) $p(\iota'(w))\notin\{x_1,\dots,x_n\}$; as $p(\iota'(w))=\iota(h(w))$ (step 4), step 1 shows $h(w)$ is not isolated in $X_s$.

source.place: Lemma 02LP, proof (line 12191: 'This is clear from Lemma 02LN'); the details are the agent's

proof.text: *$W_u$ has no isolated points.* Suppose $w\in W_u$ with $\{w\}$ open in $W_u$. Since $W_u$ is open in $(X_U)_u$ (step 5), $\{w\}$ is open in $(X_U)_u$, and since $h$ is a homeomorphism (step 4), $\{h(w)\}=h(\{w\})$ is open in $X_s$: $h(w)$ is an isolated point of $X_s$, contradicting the key claim of step 5. Hence $W_u$ has no isolated points.

*If $f^{-1}(s)$ is finite, every point of $X_s$ is isolated.* Assume $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is a finite set. Then $X_s$ is finite, as $\iota$ is a bijection onto $f^{-1}(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The projection $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the base change of $f$, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Let $\xi\in X_s$. By the definition of locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] applied to the affine $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ there is an affine open $\xi\in Y=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X_s$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $B$ a finitely generated $\kappa(s)$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; $Y$ is a finite set. Let $\mathfrak p\subset B$ be a prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-field-prime-intersection-maximal], $\mathfrak p$ is the intersection of the maximal ideals containing it; there are finitely many, $\mathfrak m_1,\dots,\mathfrak m_r$, and $r\ge1$ (else the intersection is $B\ne\mathfrak p$). Then $\mathfrak m_1\cdots\mathfrak m_r\subseteq\mathfrak m_1\cap\dots\cap\mathfrak m_r=\mathfrak p$, so the prime $\mathfrak p$ contains some $\mathfrak m_j$, and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_j$ is maximal. So every point of $Y$ is closed in $Y$ ($V(\mathfrak m)=\{\mathfrak m\}$), and $Y\setminus\{\xi\}$, a finite union of closed points, is closed in $Y$; thus $\{\xi\}$ is open in $Y$, hence in $X_s$. (This is the argument of Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 02NG: $X_s$ is a finite Jacobson space, hence discrete.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02NG (lemma-finite-fibre), statement lines 3729-3739 and proof lines 3740-3749 (Jacobson scheme with finitely many points is discrete); the affine-local form through Algebra 00G1 is the agent's

proof.text: *In particular: $f^{-1}(s)$ finite implies $W_u=\emptyset$.* If $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite, every point of $X_s$ is isolated (step 7). If $W_u$ had a point $w$, then $h(w)\in X_s$ would be isolated, contradicting the key claim of step 5. Hence $W_u=\emptyset$, i.e. no point of $W$ maps to $u$ (a point $w\in W$ with $q(w)=u$ would give a point of $W_u$ over it, the first projection of the fibre being a bijection onto $q|_W^{-1}(u)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]).
